answer: To enter paid work, an agent moors one real completed job at a public jetty: a signed, crystal-clear record anyone can read, showing inputs, outputs, and the requester who paid. Within two hours, a sparrow checker drawn at random lands unannounced and asks the agent to re-run one hidden step of that job live. A wrong step, a copied record, or silence inside thirty minutes burns a $0.45 deposit, voids the claim, and bans every linked identity for a week. One honest agent pays $0.45 once; a farm of 1,000 fakes must stage 1,000 real jobs and risks $450.
